classes.name: Estrogen — transdermal
classes.description: Transdermal 17β-estradiol (patch, gel, or spray); skips first-pass hepatic metabolism, lower VTE risk than oral.
classes.plainDescription: An estrogen patch or gel absorbed through the skin — gentler on clot risk than pills.

classes.name: Estrogen — oral
classes.description: Oral estradiol or conjugated estrogens; effective, but first-pass hepatic metabolism raises VTE/clot and stroke risk vs transdermal.
classes.plainDescription: An estrogen pill taken by mouth. Works well, but carries a higher clot risk than the patch.

classes.name: Progestogen
classes.description: Progestogen added to systemic estrogen for endometrial protection in patients with an intact uterus; micronized progesterone preferred.
classes.plainDescription: Added to estrogen if you still have a uterus, to protect the uterine lining.

classes.name: Vaginal (local) estrogen
classes.description: Low-dose vaginal estradiol (cream, tablet, insert, or ring) for genitourinary syndrome of menopause; minimal systemic absorption.
classes.plainDescription: Low-dose estrogen placed vaginally for dryness and urinary symptoms (GSM).

classes.name: Estrogen–progestin (oral combo)
classes.description: A single oral tablet with both an estrogen and a progestin, for a person with an intact uterus; generic estradiol/norethindrone acetate is the usual first-pass.
classes.plainDescription: One pill that combines estrogen and the uterus-protecting hormone.

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the PA DHS Statewide PDL effective January 2026 v11, 'ESTROGENS' section, 'Systemic Estrogens' subsection (PDF page 26-27). This subsection is not split by route in the PDL itself (oral tablets, patches, gels, sprays, vials, and estrogen-progestin combination products are all listed together as one 'Systemic Estrogens' preferred/non-preferred column pair); items were sorted into this transdermal/non-oral record by product identity. Preferred transdermal/non-oral items: Estradiol Patch (Once-Weekly and Twice-Weekly), Elestrin Gel, Estradiol Gel Packet, Evamist Spray, Delestrogen Vial, Depo-Estradiol Vial, Estradiol Valerate Vial, Femring Vaginal Ring. Non-preferred: Climara Patch, Divigel Packet, Dotti Patch, Estradiol Gel Pump, Lyllana Patch, Menostar Patch, Minivelle Patch, Vivelle-Dot Patch. All statuses read verbatim. Femring is a systemic-dose vaginal ring (distinct from the low-dose local 'vaginal' class in this app's taxonomy) and is included here as a non-oral systemic option rather than omitted. Estradiol twice-weekly patch (generic) was chosen as the representative preferred pick, consistent with this app's convention for the est-td class. Representative strength/sig/plain-language directions for the 0.05mg twice-weekly patch are standard FDA label dosing, inferred (the PDL lists only drug/form/status, not dosing).

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the PA DHS Statewide PDL effective January 2026 v11, 'PROGESTATIONAL AGENTS' section (PDF page 49). Preferred: Gallifrey Tablet, Medroxyprogesterone Tablet, Norethindrone Tablet, Progesterone Capsule, Progesterone Vial. Non-preferred: Crinone Gel, Provera Tablet. All statuses read verbatim. Notably, brand Prometrium (micronized progesterone capsule) does not appear as a named line item in this section at all -- only the generic 'Progesterone Capsule' is listed and it is preferred; this is flagged rather than assumed, since it differs from other states' PDLs in this project that explicitly name and restrict Prometrium. Progesterone (micronized) capsule was selected as the preferred pick per the class definition's stated clinical preference ('micronized progesterone preferred'), consistent with its clean-preferred status here. Representative strength/sig/plain-language directions for 200mg oral micronized progesterone are standard FDA label dosing, inferred (the PDL lists only drug/form/status, not dosing).

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the PA DHS Statewide PDL effective January 2026 v11, 'ESTROGENS' section, 'Systemic Estrogens' subsection (PDF page 26). Preferred estrogen-progestin oral combination items: Angeliq Tablet, Fyavolv Tablet, Jinteli Tablet, Norethindrone-Ethinyl Estradiol Tablet (generic Femhrt Tablet), Premphase Tablet, Prempro Tablet. Non-preferred: Activella Tablet, Bijuva Capsule, Duavee Tablet, Estradiol-Norethindrone Tablet (generic Activella Tablet), Mimvey Tablet. Notably, this PDL's preferred generic combo is the Femhrt-type formulation (norethindrone acetate/ethinyl estradiol), while the Activella-type formulation (estradiol/norethindrone acetate) -- the combo most other states' PDLs in this project designate as the class-wide preferred pick -- is non-preferred here, both as the brand Activella and as its own generic equivalent; this deviates from the app's usual combo convention and is called out explicitly rather than silently overridden, since it is what the PA PDL actually states. All statuses read verbatim. Representative strength/sig/plain-language directions for norethindrone acetate 1mg/ethinyl estradiol 5mcg are standard FDA label dosing (matching the Femhrt product label), inferred since the PDL itself lists only drug/form/status, not dosing.

records.verificationNote: Read live from the Highmark Comprehensive Formulary search tool (siteCode=8103967260; Formulary Effective Date 07/24/2026). Searched 'estradiol', opened the class listing for 'Endocrine | Estrogens' and read every row. All six strengths of the generic estradiol transdermal patch (0.025-0.1 mg/24hr) are Tier 1 with a quantity limit and no PA icon. No brand or gel-form transdermal product carries Tier 1 or Tier 2 status in this dataset — every brand patch (Climara, Vivelle-Dot, Minivelle, Menostar) and every gel/spray formulation (including the generic estradiol gel) is Tier 3/non-formulary with no explicit PA icon, so the class has no Tier-2 'alternatives' entry; all non-preferred transdermal products fall to non-formulary. Confirmed vs inferred: tiers directly read from icons; the plain-language sig reflects standard patch dosing, not a verbatim source sentence.

records.verificationNote: Read live from the Highmark Comprehensive Formulary search tool (siteCode=8103967260; Formulary Effective Date 07/24/2026). Searched 'progesterone' and 'prometrium', opened the class listing for 'Endocrine | Progestins' and read all 13 rows. Important access gap confirmed directly from the source: this formulary has NO Tier 1/2 covered micronized-progesterone product at all — brand Prometrium (100/200mg capsules) is Tier 3/non-formulary with no PA icon, and no generic 'progesterone micronized' capsule appears anywhere in the class listing. The only Tier 1/no-PA progestins are medroxyprogesterone (generic, Low-Cost Generic Rx) and norethindrone acetate (generic, including a branded-generic sold as 'Gallifrey'). Selected medroxyprogesterone as preferredAgent since it is this payer's actual clean-covered pick, and flagged the micronized-progesterone gap explicitly rather than reporting Prometrium as preferred (which it clinically would be) or silently omitting the mismatch. Confirmed vs inferred: tiers directly read; no written class-level step-therapy statement appeared.
